summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-base preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall: node setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13), unpacks it to a temp directory, chmods +x, and executes a sibling file math_init.js under that newly-fetched interpreter. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file (mangled identifiers, large numeric/string constant array, string-array-rotation decoder) that is not referenced by the package's declared main (index.js) and has no relation to a Babel preset. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers and string-map indirection hiding calls to execFileSync, https.get, fs.readFileSync('/etc/os-release'), and chmod. Installing the package causes an alternate-runtime interpreter to execute attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's machine at install time; the alternate-runtime pattern also evades Node-based static analyzers. The advertised purpose (a Babel preset) requires none of this behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
